title: Reject stale plan approvals with an expectedPlanRevision on approve
description: MoeCommandSender.approveTask(taskId) sends only the task id, and the daemon approve path (taskStore / WebSocketServer) checks status, not which plan revision the human saw. The JetBrains PlanReviewDialog builds DoD and steps once and rerenders only comments on later updates, so a newer submit_plan can be approved from a dialog still showing the old plan. Add a monotonically increasing plan revision to the task (bumped on every submit_plan), accept expectedPlanRevision on the approve command (WS message from the plugins and the MCP tool if one exists), reject with a structured error when it does not match the current revision, and make the JetBrains dialog either rerender the plan on a revision change or disable Approve with a 'plan changed — refresh' notice. VS Code: send the revision too (small). Source: roadmap 2026-09-10 §4 'Fix approval freshness'.
definitionOfDone: task.planRevision exists in docs/SCHEMA.md and is bumped by submit_plan (vitest)
Approve with a stale expectedPlanRevision returns a structured error and leaves the task in AWAITING_APPROVAL (vitest); approve without the field keeps working for old clients
JetBrains PlanReviewDialog sends expectedPlanRevision and cannot approve a plan it has not rendered (JUnit test on the dialog model or presenter)
VS Code approve command sends expectedPlanRevision
./gradlew test and daemon npm test green

implementationPlan.description: CROSS-LAYER INTEGRATION TEST. Explicit error handling coverage is the point of this step: every refusal, malformed token, disconnected client and teardown path gets an asserted outcome. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/server/planApproval.integration.test.ts using the real-dispatch pattern already established in src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts and the compare-and-swap child's planApproval.test.ts: a real http server on port 0, a real StateManager over a disposable temp project, a real McpAdapter and real ws clients, under CONTROL approval mode. Never call a private handler directly and never race two direct calls; anything not driven over a socket goes through state.runExclusive, which is how production reaches the store. The cases here are the ones NO single child could own, so do not re-run a child's whole matrix: a review client A snapshots revision N over the plugin socket while client B submits a newer plan over the MCP socket, and A's later approval at N is refused with the exact code, codeName and detail keys recorded in step 1, leaving the task AWAITING_APPROVAL with unchanged persisted bytes, timestamps, assignment, activity and no approval event; A then refreshes to N+1 and approves successfully. Repeat that shape for the OTHER two writers the centralized stamp covers, since only an integration test crosses them: a real amend_plan_step, and a real plugin UPDATE_TASK edit of steps or the Definition of Done. Prove the one-bump rule end to end - both surfaces changed in one write advances once, a byte-identical full resubmit advances once, an equal sanitized edit and a comments-only change advance not at all. Prove durability by reloading a fresh StateManager and approving with the reloaded revision. Prove backwards compatibility: an omitted token still approves, and a legacy record with no stored stamp approves at explicit 0. Cover both approval routes, a malformed present token, a forged revision inside an update patch, and a serialized newer-submit-before-older-approval race. Assert observable refusal and state, never source ordering or a helper only the test calls. Red proof: revert the fence or the bump in an ISOLATED SCRATCH COPY outside the shared checkout, record which cases fail, and restore it before the gate - never mutate the shared tree, which peers are working in. In afterEach or finally, close every ws client, close the server, cancel timers and remove only the test-owned temp directory, on every operating system.
implementationPlan.note:
CREATED packages/moe-daemon/src/server/planApproval.integration.test.ts (new, 859 lines, 15 tests, 1 top-level describe / 4 groups). No production file touched.

REAL-DISPATCH FIXTURE (same pattern as src/server/planApproval.test.ts + WebSocketServer.test.ts): real http server on port 0, real StateManager over an mkdtemp project, real McpAdapter, real MoeWebSocketServer, genuine ws clients on BOTH endpoints (/ws plugin + /mcp JSON-RPC), CONTROL approval mode. No private handler is called and no two direct calls are raced — every mutation goes over a socket, so the daemon's own mutex serializes it exactly as in production. Frames are matched by CONTENT (`nextFrame`/`nextOfType` with a payload predicate), never by arrival order, because every write emits both a reply and a broadcast; the connect-time STATE_SNAPSHOT is consumed inside connectPlugin so a later read is never the stale one.

CASES (cross-layer only — no child matrix is re-run):
(1) reviewer vs a concurrent writer, one per WRITER: newer `moe.submit_plan` over /mcp; real `moe.amend_plan_step` over /mcp; a second plugin client's UPDATE_TASK DoD edit; plus the UPDATE_TASK drag approval route. Each asserts the exact refusal recorded in step 1 (code -32002, codeName PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH, context EXACTLY {taskId, expectedPlanRevision, currentPlanRevision}, operation APPROVE_TASK/UPDATE_TASK), task still AWAITING_APPROVAL, unchanged persisted BYTES (whole-file compare covers updatedAt + assignment), planApprovedAt still absent, and no PLAN_APPROVED/PLAN_AUTO_APPROVED activity — then a refresh at N+1 approves.
(2) one-bump rule end to end: both surfaces in one write = +1; byte-identical full resubmit = +1; equal sanitized edit = no bump AND the rendered token still approves; comments-only (`moe.add_comment`) = no bump AND the rendered token still approves (the JetBrains "comments rerender" scenario, proven at the daemon).
(3) durability + legacy: stop the server, reload a FRESH StateManager over the same bytes, restart — reloaded revision approves, pre-restart one is refused; a stamp-less legacy row still approves with the key OMITTED; a stamp-less row bumped by a wire edit refuses 0 and accepts 1.
(4) error paths: numeric-looking STRING token -> -32602 INVALID_INPUT with context EXACTLY {taskId} (no revision leak) and unchanged bytes; a forged planRevision/expectedPlanRevision riding inside a patch that LEGITIMATELY changes the DoD is stripped and the derived bump wins (99 refused, 8 accepted); a reviewer that closes its socket right after a refused approval leaves the task untouched and a second client still approves; a serialized amend-vs-approve race asserts BOTH consistent outcomes strictly (never an arrival order) and that the counter advanced exactly once either way.

GREEN (shared checkout): `npx vitest run src/server/planApproval.integration.test.ts` -> Test Files 1 passed, Tests 15 passed, EXIT=0, 2.80s. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` -> EXIT=0.

RED PROOF, taken ONLY in an isolated scratch copy (`git worktree add -f .worktrees/parent-redproof HEAD`, node_modules junctioned, test file copied in; the shared tree was never mutated). Four mutations of packages/moe-daemon/src/state/taskStore.ts, each restored from a %TEMP% pristine copy before the next:
- fence off (`if (false && expectedPlanRevision !== undefined)`) -> 9 failed / 6 passed, EXIT=1
- bump off (derivePlanRevision always returns current) -> 10 failed / 5 passed, EXIT=1
- bump always (no-op predicate disabled) -> 4 failed / 11 passed, EXIT=1 (kills both no-op guards)
- omission treated as a token (`if (true)`) -> 1 failed / 14 passed, EXIT=1 (kills the legacy-omit guard)
Union = 15/15 tests killed by at least one mutation: no case is decorative. Scratch cleanup verified: junction removed with (Get-Item).Delete() (never a recursive delete through it), `packages/moe-daemon/node_modules/vitest` still present, worktree directory removed and `git worktree prune` run, `git worktree list` no longer shows it.

implementationPlan.description: DOCUMENT THE FEATURE, CORRECT THE CONTRACT DOCS. Create docs/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS.md as the one cross-client, user-visible note this feature has: what changed and why, plus a deterministic reproduction checklist a human can run - open the JetBrains review at revision N, change steps or the Definition of Done to N+1 WITHOUT touching comments, observe approve latched disabled with the close-and-reopen notice, reopen and review N+1; in VS Code, a click queued at N during the render debounce never silently upgrades to an unseen N+1, and the token advances only after a completed render. implementationPlan.note:
WHOLE-FEATURE ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of the six child diffs plus this parent's test+docs diff, read as one feature. Every item below was checked against source, not against a summary.

CONFIRMED
1. Counter never regresses, never double-bumps. `derivePlanRevision` returns `current` or `current + 1` and nothing else, is called exactly once per `updateTask`, and the stamp is placed AFTER the `...finalUpdates` spread so a caller value can never win. No writer bypasses that choke point: amendPlanStep -> state.updateTask; WS UPDATE_TASK -> state.updateTask; submitPlan -> state.updateTask; the three direct writers (orphan-parent clear, reorderTask, worker purge) all spread `...task` and never touch the surface. A sanitized no-op really is a no-op on every writer — proven end to end by the equal-edit and comments-only cases.
2. Comparison is under the real mutex and strictly before any side effect. `approveTask` order is getTask -> AWAITING_APPROVAL check -> token validate -> compare -> `cancelSpeedModeTimeout` -> `updateTask`; both /ws routes call it inside `withMutex`. A refusal leaves bytes (whole-file compare), cache, updatedAt, assignment, activity and the pending SPEED timer untouched — asserted behaviourally, not by reading source order.
3. No forged stamp or command metadata is persisted from any client. `UPDATE_TASK_DENYLIST` carries both `planRevision` and `expectedPlanRevision`, `updateTask` deletes a caller `planRevision`, and the token is read from the PAYLOAD not from `updates`. The new integration case proves it in the nastiest shape: a forged 99 riding inside a patch that legitimately changes the DoD — the derived bump (8) wins, 99 is refused, and neither key reaches disk.
4. One contract everywhere. -32002 / `PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH` with `{taskId, expectedPlanRevision, currentPlanRevision}`, -32602 / `INVALID_INPUT` with no revision numbers, identical in taskStore, WebSocketServer's allowlist, the VS Code onError promotion, the JetBrains error path and both docs.
5. Numeric domain matches with NO narrowing. Daemon: `Number.isSafeInteger` / `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`. Kotlin: `Task.planRevision: Long?` + `MAX_SAFE_PLAN_REVISION = 9007199254740991L`, parsed via `BigDecimal(...).longValueExact()`; grep over moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin for `toInt`/`asInt` on any revision symbol returns NOTHING. VS Code: `Number.isSafeInteger`, no coercion.
6. JetBrains ordering holds. `approval.onStateUpdate(...)` runs FIRST in `onState` — before the `oldComments == newComments` early return and outside the 200 ms debounce — so a steps/DoD change with byte-identical comments still invalidates. `Decision.Send` carries only the captured revision and `sendApproval` passes `send.expectedPlanRevision`; the PENDING latch disarms the button before the command goes out, so two clicks send once; a transport success never closes the dialog.
7. VS Code binds to a COMPLETED render. `rendered` only moves after the try/catch render; a different revision latches with a persistent reopen notice, so a click queued at N never becomes an approval at N+1; the panel forwards the supplied token verbatim, never reads `currentState`, and refuses a missing/malformed token WITHOUT the one-argument legacy fallback; `contentOutOfSync` fails closed; the debounce timer is cleared on dispose.
8. Both clients refuse while disconnected, on a deleted task and on a changed status, and stay usable after a send failure or daemon error (JetBrains: notConnected / taskMissing / statusChanged / revisionUnusable / notRendered / sendFailed / daemonError; VS Code: warning + reportApprovalFailure on each path).
9. An omitted token still approves for old clients — asserted at the store, on both wire routes, and now on a legacy stamp-less row over the wire.
10. No child test was weakened or deleted to make this gate pass: `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only e8764e5..HEAD` lists NOTHING, and test churn across the epic is +10770/-5 with the only 5 deleted lines in `claimNextTask.contract.test.ts`, an unrelated peer task's file.

FIXED BY THIS REVIEW (my own new file, then re-gated)
- `nextMessage` armed a 5 s timeout per frame read and never cleared it on delivery — a green suite that still keeps a worker's event loop busy long after the test. Now the timer is cleared when the frame is delivered. `npx tsc --noEmit` EXIT=0 and the FULL gate was re-run on those final bytes (evidence below).

DISCLOSED, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE
- A SPEED callback already queued behind the state mutex can still auto-approve after a human refusal. The CAS governs the approval command, not a timer already in the queue. Accepted by that slice's QA; now documented as a boundary.
- Two error-detail-key spellings (`currentRevision` on PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED, `currentPlanRevision` on PLAN_REVISION_MISMATCH). Documented in both docs; renaming a shipped key would break downstream parsers.
- FOLLOW-UP CANDIDATE (child-owned, NOT fixable inside this parent's four-file scope): slice 4's QA recorde
